findings.title: Recorded denials pin a deny for 30s, bypassing the new requery and surviving grants
findings.body: Check consults permDenialCache before anything else and returns Allowed=false on a hit, without consulting the permission cache or the DB. Entries are written whenever a DB-backed check denies (line 154) and are removed only by the 30s TTL; nothing clears them when a grant is written or a resource is created. The requery added by this PR only runs on a permission-cache miss, so a denial recorded before the creator's permission was visible (for example a GET racing the permission write, or any read of the UID before it existed) keeps returning denied for up to 30 seconds. That is the exact symptom the PR says it fixes, so the fix is incomplete for that window.

findings.title: Denial cache key is ambiguous: different resources can collide
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey joins name and parent folder with '_' without escaping. Grafana UIDs can contain underscores, so the tuple is ambiguous: dashboard 'a_b' in folder 'c' and dashboard 'a' in folder 'b_c' both produce '...perm_<uid>_<action>_a_b_c'. A denial recorded for one resource then makes Check return denied for the other for 30s without consulting permissions. The result is false denials of legitimate access for the feature this PR targets. Encode the tuple unambiguously (length-prefixed fields, a JSON array, or a hash of the tuple).

findings.title: Requery on permission-cache miss still reads a stale folder tree
findings.body: The requery only refreshes the permission set. checkInheritedPermissions (line 590) calls buildFolderTree, which returns the folderCache entry for up to 30s with no bypass. A folder created in that window is missing from the tree, so its ancestors cannot be resolved and a user whose access is inherited from an ancestor folder is denied for resources inside it. That denial is then cached (line 154). The requery therefore does not cover inherited access to newly created folders, and no test covers this case because the folder tests seed a complete tree.

findings.title: Every unmatched name now triggers an uncached permissions query
findings.body: On a permission-cache miss for a name, which is the normal case for any resource the user cannot access, Check always runs the uncached GetUserPermissions query. Before this PR those denials were answered from the cached permission map with no DB access. The denial cache is keyed by exact (action, name, folder), so a caller checking many distinct names the user cannot access costs one DB permissions query per name per 30s. The DB cost of this path should be considered or documented.

findings.title: Explicit denial-cache test passes without the denial cache
findings.body: The test is meant to show the denial entry short-circuits the check, but it cannot fail if that logic is removed. The permission cache entry for dash1 is set to false (line 982), so checkPermission returns false, and the DB fallback also denies because setupService's fakeStore has no userPermissions. The result is false with or without permDenialCache. The comment 'Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked' contradicts the value set. Set the cached permission for dash1 to true so only the denial entry produces the deny, and/or assert the store was not called. No test also checks that a DB-confirmed denial actually populates permDenialCache.

findings.title: List has no requery path, so newly created items stay out of results for up to 30s
findings.body: List answers from the 30s permission-map entry on a hit and never requeries, because it cannot tell which resources are missing from the cached set. Dashboards and folders created by the user therefore stay absent from list results for up to 30 seconds, the same class of problem this PR claims to fix for Check. The PR does not mention or test this limitation.
